newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian telecoms chief named in corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Italian telecoms chief named in corruption probe.

text.p: The head of Italy's state telecommunications holding Stet and the third highest official in the tax police were told on Thursday they were under investigation in a corruption probe, RAI television reported.

The state television, quoting judicial sources, said Stet managing director Ernesto Pascale and tax police chief-of-staff Nicolo Pollari were placed under investigation by magistrates in the northwestern town of Aosta.
Magistrates allege Pascale was involved with a secret group set up to try to influence public and government appointments in contravention of a 1982 law passed after the P2 scandal.
P2 -- "Propaganda Two" -- was the name of an illegal masonic lodge which counted government and senior state officials in its ranks and was alleged to have operated as a "state within a state".

RAI noted that Lorenzo Necci, the former head of the state railway company who is in prison after being arrested last month, was also under investigation into an alleged corrupt "super lobby" in state industries and the judiciary.
Pollari was under investigation as an accessory. The deputy head of the tax police, Michele Mola, was recently placed under investigation for the same offence, Italian media reported.
Magistrates allege that both tax police officials tipped off a member of the separatist Northern League party that his telephone was bugged.

"I'm flabbergasted," Pascale said in a statement. "I can't even imagine what hypothesis this investigation is based on. There's never been anything secret in my life and I am sure that this can demonstrated as quickly as possible."
